posts.title: I’m Back, and I’ve Been Building TimeStitcher
posts.description: It’s been a long time since I posted here. I’ve still been building software, and lately I’ve been focused on TimeStitcher, a productivity app for capturing working thoughts and seeing how they develop over time. The idea is simple: Capture thoughts fast. See how they evolve. TimeStitcher captures thoughts in “stitches,” which can be rearranged, searched, and revisited later. A stitch might hold a daily todo, a rough idea, a project fragment, a client note, a research note, or any piece of thinking that does not fit neatly into a separate file. Most note apps save the latest version of what you write. TimeStitcher is designed to preserve the path your thinking took over time: what you wrote, what changed, when it changed, and what might matter later. I built it because I wanted a place where I could keep many notes visible together, move quickly between ideas, recover earlier thinking when something I deleted turned out to matter, and track the active time I spent on each stitch. posts.title: How An Interview Became Free Consulting
posts.description: Here is an entertaining story I think you will enjoy. But there is a lesson: protect yourself from being used as I was. TL;DR: Insist on a two-way NDA. True story, this happened to me last week. I got a call about a consulting job: a 3-6 month contract for a Windows Visual C++ Developer, full-time at an hourly rate. The company was reluctant to express any limits for the hourly rate — price did not seem to matter to them. The interview was on a gorgeous Friday before Labor Day weekend. At the appointed time, I arrived and was greeted by the president of the startup. I liked him right away. We were the same ages and exchanged tidbits of raising a family in the Bay Area. He explained that his company produced a limited number of high cost medical devices. An updated, smaller model was announced earlier in the year, and it was due to the first customers in a month.
